Field notes

Introducing Atomic: from idea to application

Meet Atomic, a new way to build and refine web apps through conversation. Early-access requests are open.

Abstract Machines · 27 October 2026 · 3 min read

On this pageWhy we’re building AtomicStart with a conversationKeep building from thereHelp shape what comes next

Why we’re building Atomic

Good ideas for software often come from people who understand a problem firsthand. A founder sees a better way to serve customers. A small team needs a tool that fits the way it works. A developer has a product idea and wants to find out if people will use it.

Yet getting from an idea to something people can try still takes time and technical work. At Abstract Machines, we’re building Atomic to make that first step easier. Today, we’re introducing it and inviting people to request early access.

Start with a conversation

Tell Atomic what you want to build, who it’s for, and what those people need to do. Atomic generates a web application you can preview. From there, you can describe what needs to change and build another version. The first result gives you something concrete to react to.

It might be a customer portal, an internal tool, or the first version of a new product. Seeing an app take shape while the idea is still fresh helps you decide what it really needs.

Keep building from there

The first preview is a beginning. Builders can inspect generated source, review verified versions, and choose a version to publish. That gives you a way to understand and improve the app as your idea develops.

Atomic builds on Atom, Abstract Machines’ open-source foundation for identity, permissions, and data. A useful app needs those pieces as well as an interface. As with any generated software, review and test your app before using it with real customers or important data.

Help shape what comes next

We’re starting with a limited number of builders so we can learn from the people using Atomic. We want to see what you try to make, where the experience helps, and where it gets in your way. We’ll review requests and invite selected people in batches as the product develops.

Requesting access does not create a Builder account or guarantee an invitation. If you have an idea you want to try, tell us what it is, who would use it, and how you handle that work today. We’d love to hear about it.

Tell us your idea and request early access ↗
